account:
It is day 1, just after noon, and I have returned home for my scheduled lunch. Today's unusual matter is a rumour about a bridge or port change associated with the bakery. Townsfolk at the mill repeated it; one said the baker, innkeeper and neighbour had been there. I did not witness that conversation, and I do not know what change, if any, anyone intends. The secretary reported no actual proposal or correspondence on the subject, so I should not treat the rumour as an official plan or decision. I can seek firsthand clarification when an opportunity arises, including at my fifteen hundred tea with the neighbour.

This morning's scheduled mill grain inspection was incomplete. I attended and asked for the miller, grain quantities, storage conditions and supply concerns, but located neither the miller nor stock records. I recorded that limitation rather than claiming findings. At my thirteen hundred office appointment for council letters, I intend to ask the secretary to arrange another inspection with the miller present and records available.

The builder has requested an eighteen hundred inspection of completed great hall lighting. The secretary needed a writable book because the original appointment book was signed; I supplied one, and the secretary recorded a signed addendum. That appears to be ordinary scheduling for checking the builder's work, not evidence of a connection to the bakery rumour. I also have the usual fifteen hundred dockside tea and sixteen-thirty office appointment before the lighting inspection.
